name: Example: Determining Whether Two Events are Mutually Exclusive
problem: Given $P(A)=\dfrac{1}{3},$ $P(B)=\dfrac{1}{4},$ and $P(A\cup B)=\dfrac{7}{12},$ determine whether $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events.
worked_solution:
To check if $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive, we must check that $P(A\cap B) = 0.$

We can calculate $P(A\cap B)$ using the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ \frac{7}{12} & =\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{4}-P(A\cap B) \\ P(A\cap B) & =\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{4}-\frac{7}{12} \\  & =\frac{4+3-7}{12} \\  & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events.
